opening: This application has no access controls that work: any caller from the internet can take over any user account, run arbitrary commands on the server, or read every secret the service depends on — without supplying any credential. The service must not be publicly reachable in its current state.
bullets_intro: What an attacker can do today:

bullets.title: Authentication bypassed at login
bullets.body: Database query injection (SQL injection) at the login handler grants any caller a signed admin session without a password.

bullets.title: Server takeover via admin route
bullets.body: Command string injection (OS command injection) on an unauthenticated admin route lets any caller run arbitrary system commands.

bullets.title: All runtime secrets exposed
bullets.body: An unauthenticated debug route returns all runtime configuration as plain text, disclosing every credential and signing secret used by the application.

bullets.title: Account access freely forgeable
bullets.body: The session signing key is committed in source code so any reader with repository access can issue tokens for any user identity.

bullets.title: Customer account data exposed
bullets.body: User records are readable without authentication, exposing account details and role assignments for any enumerated identifier.

bullets.title: AI assistant open to cost abuse
bullets.body: The AI assistant accepts unauthenticated requests with no rate limit, enabling cost exhaustion and prompt manipulation against the integrated language model.

closing: Adding authentication to every public route and removing all hardcoded secrets would close the most critical risks; the remaining gaps follow from those two absent controls.
